questions.question: Which instrument belongs to the string family?
How does a violin typically produce sound?
choices: A bowed or plucked string vibrates

questions.question: Which is a woodwind instrument?
How does a brass player usually change pitch?
choices: By changing lip vibration and using valves or a slide

questions.question: Which instrument is an example of percussion?
What is the main sound source in a flute?
choices: A reed vibrating against a mouthpiece

questions.question: Which instrument uses a double reed?
What distinguishes a trombone from most brass instruments?
choices: It is played with a bow
A slide is used to change the tube length

questions.question: Which family does the piano commonly belong to in orchestral classification?
choices: Keyboard, though its sound is produced by struck strings

questions.question: Why can instruments in the same family have different timbres?
choices: They vary in size, materials, shape, and playing technique
They are made for different audiences only

questions.question: Which instrument is a low-pitched member of the string family?
What is a reed's role in many woodwind instruments?
choices: It changes the instrument's length electronically
It vibrates to set the air column in motion

questions.question: Which instrument is commonly played by striking tuned bars?
What makes a timpani different from an untuned drum?
choices: Its pitch can be adjusted to specific notes
It is played with a bow

questions.question: A sound begins with air blown through a cup-shaped mouthpiece. Which family is likely?
Why does an orchestra use instruments with different ranges?
choices: They ensure every part is a solo
They eliminate the need for balance
They can perform complementary high, middle, and low musical roles

questions.question: Which instrument is a free-reed instrument?
How does a harp create sound?
choices: A metal tube resonates when shaken

questions.question: What should a listener notice when comparing instrument families?
choices: How sound is produced and how timbre differs

questions.question: Why is instrument classification sometimes flexible?
choices: Some instruments combine features or fit different teaching and performance groupings
